levels.title: Earth, Weather & Climate in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how Earth's rock, air, water and life link into one system that shapes weather and climate.

levels.title: What Makes a Mineral?
levels.objective: After this level you can tell a mineral from a rock and list the traits every mineral shares, from a set recipe to an orderly crystal.

levels.title: Testing a Mineral
levels.objective: After this level you can identify a mineral by its hardness, streak and luster, using the Mohs scale.

levels.title: Quartz, Feldspar and Mica
levels.objective: After this level you can name the most common minerals in Earth's crust and spot them in everyday granite and sand.

levels.title: Rocks Born From Fire
levels.objective: After this level you can tell granite from basalt and explain why slow cooling grows bigger crystals.

levels.title: Rocks Made of Layers
levels.objective: After this level you can recognize sandstone, shale and limestone and say what each one started out as.

levels.title: Rocks Remade by Heat
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how heat and pressure turn limestone into marble and shale into slate.

levels.title: Gems and Ores
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what makes a mineral a gem and what makes a rock an ore worth mining.

levels.title: Soil: More Than Dirt
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what soil is made of and name the layers you would see in a soil pit.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Rocks and Minerals
levels.objective: After this level you can sort any common rock into igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic and explain the minerals inside it.

levels.title: The Heat Inside the Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain where Earth's inner heat comes from and why it keeps the planet active.

levels.title: Three Ways Plates Meet
levels.objective: After this level you can name divergent, convergent and transform plate boundaries and give a real example of each.

levels.title: Hotspots: Hawaii and Yellowstone
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a hotspot is and why it leaves a chain of volcanoes as a plate moves over it.

levels.title: Faults: Where Rock Breaks
levels.objective: After this level you can tell normal, reverse and strike-slip faults apart by which way the rock moves.

levels.title: Seismic Waves
levels.objective: After this level you can tell P waves, S waves and surface waves apart and say which kind does the most damage.

levels.title: The San Andreas Fault
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the plate boundary running through California and why it builds up large quakes.

levels.title: Why the Same Quake Shakes Unevenly
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how distance, depth and soft ground, including liquefaction, change how hard a place shakes.

levels.title: Shield, Cone and Stratovolcano
levels.objective: After this level you can tell the three main kinds of volcano apart and link each one to runny or sticky magma.

levels.title: Lava, Ash and Pyroclastic Flows
levels.objective: After this level you can name what an eruption releases and explain why pyroclastic flows are the deadliest.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Plates, Quakes and Volcanoes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a plate boundary, fault or hotspot means for the quakes and eruptions a place can expect.

levels.title: How Rock Falls Apart
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how frost, roots and slightly acidic rain break solid rock down through weathering.

levels.title: How Caves and Sinkholes Form
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how slightly acidic groundwater dissolves limestone into caves, stalactites and sinkholes.

levels.title: How Rivers Carve Valleys
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a river erodes, carries and drops sediment, cutting V-shaped valleys and meanders.

levels.title: How Rivers Build New Land
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how floodplains and deltas form where a river slows down and drops its load.

levels.title: How Glaciers Sculpt Mountains
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how moving ice carves U-shaped valleys, cirques and fjords.

levels.title: How Wind Shapes Deserts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how wind builds dunes, strips away sand and sandblasts rock.

levels.title: How Landslides Happen
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how slope, water and gravity combine to send rock and soil sliding downhill.

levels.title: How Arches and Hoodoos Form
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how uneven erosion of hard and soft rock leaves arches, hoodoos and mesas.

levels.title: How Mountains Rise and Wear Down
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why old ranges like the Appalachians are low while young ones like the Himalayas are high.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Shaping the Land
levels.objective: After this level you can trace how water, ice, wind and gravity turn rock into the landscapes you see.

levels.title: Hutton Discovers Deep Time
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how James Hutton read tilted rock layers to argue that Earth is immensely old.

levels.title: How Rock Layers Tell Order
levels.objective: After this level you can use superposition and cross-cutting to put rock layers and events in order.

levels.title: Index Fossils: Nature's Timestamps
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how short-lived, widespread fossils let geologists match rock layers across continents.

levels.title: How Radioactive Clocks Date Rocks
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how uranium-lead dating gives a rock's age in years and why carbon dating cannot.

levels.title: How Old Is the Earth?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how meteorites and ancient zircon crystals pin Earth's age at about 4.5 billion years.

levels.title: The Geologic Time Scale
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how eons, eras and periods divide Earth's history and where humans appear on it.

levels.title: How Life Filled the Air With Oxygen
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how ancient microbes caused the Great Oxidation Event and how rocks record it.

levels.title: How Supercontinents Come and Go
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the supercontinent cycle, in which continents gather, split apart and gather again.

levels.title: How Coal, Oil and Gas Formed
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how buried plants and plankton became coal, oil and natural gas over millions of years.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Deep Time
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how geologists read rocks, fossils and radioactive clocks to tell Earth's 4.5-billion-year story.

levels.title: What Air Is Made Of
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why air is mostly nitrogen and oxygen and why tiny amounts of other gases still matter.

levels.title: The Layers of the Sky
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why temperature falls, then rises, as you climb through the atmosphere's layers.

levels.title: Why the Air Thins as You Climb
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what air pressure is and why it drops the higher you go.

levels.title: Why Rising Air Cools
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why air cools as it rises and expands, and why mountaintops are cold.

levels.title: The Ozone Layer
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the ozone layer thinned and how the Montreal Protocol is helping it recover.

levels.title: Why the Sky Is Blue
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why air scatters blue light and why sunsets turn red and orange.

levels.title: The Greenhouse Effect, Up Close
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why carbon dioxide and water vapor trap heat while nitrogen and oxygen let it pass.

levels.title: Earth's Energy Budget
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how sunlight in, heat out and reflectiveness (albedo) set Earth's temperature.

levels.title: Why Winds Curve
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Earth's spin deflects moving air (the Coriolis effect) and why storms spin.

levels.title: Milestone: A Planet Always Changing
levels.objective: After this level you can connect rocks, moving plates, erosion, deep time and the air into one picture of a planet that never sits still.

levels.title: Humidity and the Dew Point
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why warm air can hold more water vapor and what the dew point tells you.

levels.title: Why Clouds Form
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why rising air cools to its dew point and condenses on tiny specks of dust and salt.

levels.title: Reading the Clouds
levels.objective: After this level you can tell cumulus, stratus and cirrus clouds apart and explain what each suggests about the weather.

levels.title: Why Most Rain Starts as Snow
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how raindrops and snowflakes grow inside a cloud until they are heavy enough to fall.

levels.title: Highs and Lows
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why high pressure usually brings clear skies and low pressure brings clouds and storms.

levels.title: Air Masses
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why a large body of air takes on the temperature and moisture of the place it sits over.

levels.title: Cold Fronts and Warm Fronts
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the weather changes as a cold or warm front passes over you.

levels.title: The Three Cells That Circle Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how rising and sinking air in the Hadley cell puts rainforests at the Equator and deserts near 30 degrees.

levels.title: The Jet Stream
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why a fast river of wind high above steers storms and speeds up flights.

levels.title: Checkpoint: How Weather Works
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how heat, moisture, pressure and fronts combine to make the weather in your forecast.

levels.title: Inside a Thunderstorm
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the growing, mature and dying stages of a thunderstorm and what drives each one.

levels.title: How Lightning Charges Up
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how colliding ice builds electric charge in a cloud and why thunder follows the flash.

levels.title: How Hail Grows
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how strong updrafts keep hailstones aloft long enough to grow layer by layer.

levels.title: Supercells: Storms That Rotate
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how changing winds with height set a supercell spinning and why it spawns the strongest tornadoes.

levels.title: Tornado Alley and the EF Scale
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the central US gets so many tornadoes and how damage is used to rate them.

levels.title: Inside a Hurricane
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the eye, the eyewall and the rain bands work together in a mature hurricane.

levels.title: Why Category Isn't Everything
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Saffir-Simpson scale measures and why water, not wind, causes most hurricane deaths.

levels.title: Nor'easters and Blizzards
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how winter storms form along the US East Coast and what turns a snowstorm into a blizzard.

levels.title: Lake-Effect Snow
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how cold air crossing warm lakes dumps narrow bands of very heavy snow.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Storms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how heat, moisture and spinning air build thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes and winter storms.

levels.title: Why the Hottest Days Come Late
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the warmest weeks arrive well after the longest day of the year (seasonal lag).

levels.title: The Köppen Climate Map
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how climates are classified by temperature and rainfall and read a place's climate type.

levels.title: The Fast Carbon Cycle
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how carbon moves each year between the air, plants, soil and ocean.

levels.title: Earth's Slow Thermostat
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how rock weathering and volcanoes balance carbon dioxide over millions of years.

levels.title: Snowball Earth and Hothouse Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Earth's most extreme past climates and what the rocks tell us about them.

levels.title: Reading Ice Cores
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how air bubbles in ancient ice record 800,000 years of carbon dioxide and temperature.

levels.title: Earth's Wobbles and the Ice Ages
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how slow changes in Earth's orbit and tilt (Milankovitch cycles) pace the ice ages.

levels.title: The World of the Last Ice Age
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what the planet looked like about 20,000 years ago, when ice sheets covered much of North America.

levels.title: When Volcanoes Cool the World
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how big eruptions like Tambora and Pinatubo cooled the globe for a year or two.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Climates Past and Present
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how sunlight, orbit, carbon and volcanoes have set Earth's climate from the ice ages to today.

levels.title: The Keeling Curve
levels.objective: After this level you can read the record of carbon dioxide since 1958 and explain both its steady rise and its yearly zigzag.

levels.title: How We Know the Extra Carbon Is Ours
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the chemical fingerprints that trace the rise in carbon dioxide to fossil fuels.

levels.title: Measuring a Warming World
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how scientists build the global temperature record and what it shows since the 1800s.

levels.title: Ruling Out the Sun and Volcanoes
levels.objective: After this level you can weigh natural causes against greenhouse gases as explanations for recent warming.

levels.title: Feedbacks: Melting Ice and Water Vapor
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how melting ice and extra water vapor amplify an initial warming.

levels.title: Climate Sensitivity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how much warming scientists expect from doubling carbon dioxide and why the range is uncertain.

levels.title: Ice Sheets in Retreat
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Greenland and Antarctica are losing ice and why their slow response matters for centuries.

levels.title: Where the Emissions Come From
levels.objective: After this level you can name the main human sources of greenhouse gases, from power and transport to farming and forests.

levels.title: Extreme Weather and Attribution
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how warming shifts the odds of heat waves and downpours and how scientists test a single event.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Climate Change
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the evidence shows about recent warming, what causes it and what it is changing.

levels.title: How a Forecast Is Made
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how weather balloons, radar, satellites and computer models turn observations into a forecast.

levels.title: What a 40% Chance of Rain Means
levels.objective: After this level you can interpret a probability forecast and explain why forecasts lose skill after about a week or two.

levels.title: Watches Versus Warnings
levels.objective: After this level you can tell a watch from a warning and decide what to do for a tornado, a flood or a hurricane.

levels.title: Ready for an Earthquake
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why quakes cannot be predicted and why Drop, Cover and Hold On is the advice.

levels.title: Heat: The Quiet Killer
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why extreme heat is so dangerous, why cities run hotter, and who is most at risk.

levels.title: Floods: Turn Around, Don't Drown
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how flash floods form and why driving into floodwater is so dangerous.

levels.title: Why Wildfires Spread
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how heat, drought, wind and fuel combine to drive a wildfire and a longer fire season.

levels.title: Paris and the Climate Debate
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what the Paris Agreement aims for and the main options people argue over for cutting emissions and adapting.

levels.title: Myths About Weather and Climate
levels.objective: After this level you can spot and correct common mix-ups, from the ozone hole causing warming to a cold snap disproving it.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: Earth, Weather & Climate
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of Earth, Weather & Climate Levels 1 to 99 across the whole tree.
